title: NodeList Object
body:
Sort of *Array-like*, not quite a subclass of arrays

What `document.querySelectorAll` returns. It is iterable, it has `length`, and it indexes with
`[0]`, which is why it feels like an [[Array]] and why forgetting that it isn't one is the
course's most common error.

```js
const list = document.querySelectorAll(".box");
console.log(list.textContent);   // undefined: a NodeList has no textContent
for (let node of list) {         // this is what you want
	console.log(node.textContent);
}
```

The consequence that bites hardest: **NodeLists do not have [[Array Functions]]**. No `map`,
no `filter`, no `reduce`. `forEach` happens to exist on them, which makes the absence of the
others more confusing rather than less. Convert first if you need them:

```js
const arr = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(".box"));
const texts = arr.map(n => n.textContent);
```

A selector matching nothing gives an **empty** NodeList, not `null`, so a truthiness check
never catches a typo'd selector. Check `.length`.

Contrast [[Node Object]], which is a single node. See [[Selecting Nodes]].
